title: Error Response
description: Body of every refusal: the pairing endpoint, activation, the node list, the catalog, an action and application traffic alike. A client decides what to do from the code, never from the prose, and the HTTP status is the same decision written twice.

code.description:
What was refused. What each one means for a client:
  node_required — the request named no node; every request for a node carries X-Remote-Everything-Node.
  unauthorized — this device is not admitted, or not admitted to that node. A request that names no node of this gateway and one that names a node this device does not hold are answered the same way, so a device cannot learn which nodes exist by asking.
  invitation_denied — the invitation is unknown, spent, expired, or not the one this device is redeeming under.
  invitation_expired — the pending authorization this device is activating ran out; a new invitation is needed.
  approval_pending (HTTP 202) — the device paired and is waiting for its operator; ask again after it was approved.
  node_not_found — the gateway does not serve that node.
  app_not_found — that node runs no application with that id.
  not_found — the path does not exist.
  forbidden — a path this deployment keeps to itself.
  computer_offline — the node did not answer; it is off, asleep, or its tunnel is down.
  activation_failed — the device could not be activated; the operator has to look at the gateway.
  invalid_device_name / invalid_credential_password / invalid_body / invalid_json — the pairing request itself was malformed.
  rate_limited — too many requests from this client or overall; retry later.
  server_busy — the gateway is at its concurrent-pairing limit; retry later.
  pairing_failed — pairing failed on the gateway; the operator has to look at it.
  internal_error — the gateway failed to write its answer.
